content.text: No exclusivity obligation on IBM exists anywhere in the agreement — purchases are order-driven.

input.quote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on IBM, so it meets the preferred position. Purchasing is order-driven: Section 6.0 obliges IBM to purchase Products only "[s]ubject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement" with no requirements/volume commitment, and Section 6.1 lets IBM "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time." Searches for "exclusive", "sole supplier", requirements-from and third-party-sourcing restrictions surfaced only (i) an entire-agreement clause, (ii) MSL's exclusive remedy in the loan agreement, and (iii) restrictions running against MSL (e.g. MSL may use IBM Parts and assets solely in IBM Products), none of which restrict IBM's freedom to source from other suppliers. The IBM responsibilities list (Section 4.0) and the Supply Flexibility provisions likewise impose no minimum-share or single-source commitment. No redline required.
